title.narrative: Output 5.3. Increased capacity of Member States to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative:
1. Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security of China (MOHRSS) implemented a new national workplan to enhance China New Enterprise-based Apprenticeship on 28 December 2022. Since 2019, China New Enterprise-based Apprenticeship already trained over 2 million Chinese apprentices and will further expand. This national workplan highlights international cooperation on apprenticeship and core skills development, especially green skills and digital skills.
2. MOHRSS developed a training textbook on green skills in apprenticeship to integrate green skills into one of the general/core competency curricula of China New Enterprise-based Apprenticeship in 2022. .1. In collaboration with MOHRSS and social partners, the ILO. with funding from by J.P. Morgan continued to enhance the quality of apprenticeship and skills development in the context of the Chinese changing labour market. The ILO provided recommendations when the national workplan was drafted in October 2022. 2. The ILO supported national experts in China to develop the training textbook on green skills in apprenticeship under the guidance of MOHRSS in 2022. 3. The ILO led the initiative in collaboration with the UN agencies to promote institutional capacity building on green skills development in 2023. 4. The ILO provide capacity building to 110 institutions, including local authorities, enterprises, and TVET schools from 10 pilot cities/sectors in China on quality apprenticeship by the end of 2023.

Output 6.4. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen legislation, polices and measures to ensure equal opportunities and treatment in the world of work for persons with disabilities and other persons in vulnerable situations

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MOHRSS) has adopted tools to address discrimination at the workplace ensuring equal opportunities and treatment, including for persons living with HIV. In 2022, the Chinese Academy of Labour and Social Security (CALSS), with the support of MOHRSS, developed the comprehensive training manual "A Guide to HIV and Equal Employment in Recruitment, Retention, and Development.". The manual is aligned to ILO Convention No. 111 and Recommendation No. 200 and aims to effectively address discrimination throughout the entire employment cycle, with a specific emphasis on combating HIV-related discrimination.
MOHRSS advocated for the implementation of the tool in a national workshop on "Promoting High Quality and Full Employment" (2023). The workshop brought together key stakeholders such as national and provincial tripartite partners, representatives from private companies covering thousands of workers, one of the biggest HIV community groups providing services for PLHIV in 20 provinces in China, national and provincial Disabled Persons Federations, GBDN, and other relevant parties. As a result, further actions were urged to tackle discrimination in the workplace, such as strengthening legislation and policy implementation to protect the rights of vulnerable groups, promoting experience sharing on inclusive employment, sharing best practices among stakeholders, and continuing skill development for vulnerable groups in particular digital skills and green skills ensuring no one is left behind.
The recognition and endorsement of this tool have motivated various partners, including the Women's Network against AIDS-China, the Beijing Tongzhi Center, and the private sector to incorporate it into their training programs. The ILO, through the UN HIV Joint Program Framework, which is funded by the UN AIDS, played a crucial role in facilitating the development of the manual by identifying experts and fostering partnerships between the government and NGOs. The Office engaged the community and requested feedback to ensure the manual encompassed all views and was comprehensive and effective. The ILO also provided continuous support to constituents by sharing UNAIDS global strategies, updated information about HIV in China, and best practices from other countries, and ensured the manual was up to date and aligned with international standards. The ILO played an active role in promoting the manual to various stakeholders, such as the Disabled Persons Federation, employers from private companies, HIV community groups, the LGBTIQ+ community, other UN agencies, etc. This involved raising awareness, organizing workshops and training sessions, and encouraging organizations to incorporate the manual's content into their programs.
